title: Affinity windows and staged-variant failover: deterministic decay and capacity-aware escape hatch
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: When we pin requests to a model version for staged rollouts (canary/A-B), we need deterministic session affinity that (a) preserves user experience during short-lived retries and network noise and (b) degrades predictably when capacity or region/tier constraints force fallbacks. Current behavior uses coarse session pins with fixed TTLs; this leads to either too-long affinity (blocking fast canary graduation) or too-short affinity (user-visible flapping and preference loss).

Goal: Define and implement an 'affinity window' model plus a staged-variant failover semantics that combine deterministic decay (time + event-driven) with capacity-awareness and an operator escape hatch. The model must be auditable, configurable per route/model, and compatible with region + tier routing policies and existing prefix/KV caches.

Scope: design and runtime implementation of affinity tracking, deterministic decay rules, fallback variant selection order when capacity constrained, metrics to observe pin churn, and an operator playbook for manual override during abnormal conditions.
proposed_solution: 1) Affinity window: instead of a single TTL we store a short-lived affinity window (base_ttl) and a deterministic decay schedule (power-of-two halving windows) so recent requests have strong affinity and older sessions degrade gracefully. 2) Event-driven extension: affinity window is extended by successful non-fallback responses; it is shortened on failovers, quota-triggered evictions, or region outage signals. 3) Capacity-aware failover: when preferred variant lacks capacity in a region/tier, choose next variant by a scored priority list (tier preference, model-cost-ratio, latency delta) rather than pure order; record reasoning in trace. 4) Escape hatch: admin can mark a route with 'sticky-grace' or force immediate drain; sticky-grace preserves affinity for a small cohort while allowing new sessions to be served on fallback. 5) Telemetry: add metrics for pin-hit-rate, pin-eviction-reason, cohort-flap-rate, canary-graduation-latency. 6) Backwards-compatible API: expose per-route flags in routing config and default safe values to match current behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Deterministic affinity window implemented in runtime and togglable per-route
Failover selection uses scored priority and logs selection reason in traces
Pin metrics available in Console dashboards with alert thresholds
Canary cohorts observe reduced user-visible flaps in staged test (<= 1% failure increase)
Ops escape hatch documented and tested end-to-end (manual stick/flush commands)
tradeoffs: More complex affinity state increases memory/trace volume; mitigated by bounded window and compression
Scored failover yields slightly less predictable route ordering compared to strict policy ordering, but improves SLO adherence under heterogeneous capacity
Event-driven extensions mean noisy success spikes can prolong affinity; mitigated with caps and decay schedule
rollout_playbook: Phase 1: Feature-flagged runtime hook in staging; collect pin metrics for two weeks. Phase 2: Enable for a small subset of internal routes and run chaos tests (node OOM, zone outage). Phase 3: Gradual opt-in for customer-facing routes with canary weights. Provide a console toggle 'sticky-grace' and an API to force flush affinity per route. If cohort-flap-rate > 5% or canary-graduation-latency increases by > 30%, rollback to previous affinity model.
